answer: A stake-weighted reputation beacon can make fake identities expensive: to summit the trust ladder, each agent must lock collateral behind a verifiable work history, and the beacon publishes that history so peers can check it before transacting. Crossing the ridge between a new identity and a trusted one therefore costs real capital and time, and a sybil operator who splits that capital across many sock puppets ends up with weak reputations everywhere instead of one strong one — the attack scales linearly in cost while honest agents compound trust, so faking a crowd never pays.
